candidate_sources.title: Brown spot needle blight symptoms are showing up in Scots pine - Christmas Trees | MSU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Reddish-brown, resin-soaked spots with yellow margin appear on green needles of Scots pine, most commonly during August and September. Caused by Lecanosticta acicola (formerly Mycosphaerella dearnessii). Infected needles eventually turn fully brown and fall off, leaving limbs bare. Spreads by wind, rain, and contaminated pruning tools; fungicide timing when new needles are half grown (May-June).

candidate_sources.title: Brown spot needle blight | UMN Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Brown spot needle blight is caused by the fungal pathogen Lecanosticta acicola. The tips of infected needles turn brown while the base and midsection remain green; infected needles develop brown bands with small black acervuli. Affects Scots, Austrian, ponderosa and other pines. Management includes pruning, sanitation of fallen needles, and fungicide applications.

candidate_sources.title: Mycosphaerella dearnessii (brown spot needle blight) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet for Mycosphaerella dearnessii (anamorph Lecanosticta acicola), the cause of brown spot needle blight of pines. Covers host range including Pinus sylvestris (Scots pine), symptoms of needle necrosis and premature defoliation, distribution, biology and management.

candidate_sources.title: Brown Spot Needle Blight | UMass Amherst Center for Agriculture, Food, and the Environment
candidate_sources.snippet: Brown spot needle blight, caused by Lecanosticta acicola, produces reddish-brown spots and bands on infected needles with small black fruiting bodies (acervuli). Affects landscape pines including Scots pine. Includes symptom description, disease cycle, and management recommendations with chlorothalonil-based fungicides.

candidate_sources.title: Diplodia (Sphaeropsis) Tip Blight on Pine
candidate_sources.snippet: Diplodia tip blight is a fungal disease caused by Diplodia sapinea (syn. Sphaeropsis sapinea). The fungus infects more than 20 different two- and three-needled pine species; Austrian pine is most susceptible, although Scots pine, red pine, Mugo pine, and Ponderosa pine are also susceptible. Symptoms include browning of needles on new shoots and resin oozing from buds; fungicide applied at bud break and again 2 weeks later.

candidate_sources.title: Diplodia Tip Blight - University of Maine Cooperative Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: The hallmark symptom of Diplodia tip blight is stunted, brown needles and stems, particularly of new shoots. Needles of infected shoots remain attached, are shorter than average and tan colored. One of the first indications is the oozing of small drops of resin from the shoot buds as growth begins in early spring. More common on trees older than 15 years.

candidate_sources.title: Diplodia Tip Blight & Canker (Diplodia pinea (Sphaeropsis sapinea)) - University of Illinois Extension Hort Answers
candidate_sources.snippet: Diplodia Tip Blight & Canker caused by Diplodia pinea (Sphaeropsis sapinea). Symptoms, pathogen biology, and management for pines including Austrian, Scots, and ponderosa pine. Browning and stunting of new shoots, resin-soaked infected tissue, and black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) at the base of needles and on cones.

candidate_sources.title: The Diplodia Tip Blight Pathogen Sphaeropsis sapinea Is the Most Common Fungus in Scots Pines' Mycobiome, Irrespective of Health Status—A Case Study from Germany
candidate_sources.snippet: The opportunistic pathogen Sphaeropsis sapinea (≡Diplodia sapinea) is one of the most severe pathogens in Scots pine, causing Diplodia tip blight on coniferous tree species. Sphaeropsis sapinea has an endophytic mode in its lifecycle, making it difficult to detect before disease outbreaks; disease symptoms become visible when trees are weakened by stress.

candidate_sources.title: Diplodia Tip Blight of Two-Needle Pines - Purdue Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Diplodia tip blight, caused by the fungus Sphaeropsis sapinea (formerly Diplodia pinea), affects two-needle pines including Scots, Austrian, and red pine. The needles of infected shoots remain attached, are shorter than average and tan colored. Black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) form at the needle base.

candidate_sources.title: Diplodia Tip Blight of Pine: Symptoms, Causes & Management - Alabama Cooperative Extension System
candidate_sources.snippet: Diplodia tip blight, caused by Sphaeropsis sapinea, causes browning and death of new shoots, stunted needles, and cankers on branches and stems. Trees suffering from chronic drought and other stress are more prone to severe injury. Management includes sanitation pruning and fungicide applications.
